page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-6xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 6 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does provide one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate mixed performance characteristics. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the bottom 10%, and weak multi-core CPU performance in the bottom 25%. However, memory bandwidth read-only operations for both small and large blocks perform in the middle 50% tier, though large block write bandwidth drops to the bottom 25%. Standard computational tasks, such as Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, software compilation, and text processing, consistently register in the average tier.

Given the shared CPU architecture and lack of local storage, this instance is designed for workloads that do not require sustained, high-intensity CPU performance. It is suited for basic web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database operations, as demonstrated by its average performance in Passmark database tests and Redis SET operations. The shared resource model offers a cost-effective option for development environments, staging servers, and non-critical background processes where resource density is prioritized over dedicated CPU guarantees.
